text: Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards mandate that cars and light trucks have an improved fuel economy from 28.5 mi/gal (2012) to 54.5 mi/gal (2025). Weight reduction of vehicles is the key to enhancing fuel economy and reducing their carbon footprint. Glass fiber (GF) and carbon fiber (CF) composites are increasingly used in automotive components. Sheet molding compounds (SMC) [3] consist of GF or CF reinforcement (>25 mm length) impregnated between bi-layer thermoset resin. SMC provides excellent part reproducibility 1 with the desired surface finish (Class A or matte) in a commercially viable process. SMC has various fillers such as calcium carbonate and alumina trihydrate, generally added to reduce cost and improve chemical properties and heat resistance. Thermoset resins such as polyester (PE), vinyl ester (VE), epoxy and phenolics are used in SMC manufacturing. VE has higher thermal and mechanical properties compared to PE. In addition, VE offers high resistance to hydrolysis, resulting in excellent chemical resistance. VE (density 1.2 g/cm3 and tensile strength/ modulus ~ 75 MPa and 3.2 GPa, respectively) possesses hydroxyl groups along with ester chains, allowing hydrogen bonds to form with GF sizing chemistry, resulting in better wet out enhanced adhesion with GF. Commercial SMC is supplied in various fiber content, fiber orientation and formulations. GF SMC is cost effective because the part cost increases by just 1% to 1.5% with weight reduction of 25% to 35% compared to high-strength steel. SMC composites are mass produced by compression molding of the charge into the part shape. Table 1 summarizes efforts by OEMs to replace metallic parts such as aluminum, magnesium with SMC composites for lightweight in seat back rests, lift gates etc. The subject of the present work is an SMC automotive seat back rest. Seat backs are generally made of aluminum, injection- molded plastic with local GF reinforcements, magnesium, or other materials. Table 1. Use of SMC parts in automotive industries. Manufacturer and Model SMC in automotive parts Box sides, tailgate, cargo lid, headboard Honda Ridgeline Toyota Tacoma In-bed trunk assemblies Ford SportTrac Jeep Wrangler Multi piece SMC roof assemblies Nissan Sentra Trunk divider and trunk liner SMC Basics SMC is a process to produce intermediates with fiber reinforcements saturated with thermoset resins. Glass, carbon, Kevlar, basalt and other types of fiber roving are guided through individual poly vinyl chloride (PVC) tubing to a cutting module. The cutter is generally a pair of rolls, one with the helical blades and the other being a contact roll. A pressure roll is also used to keep the fibers under uniform tension. The rovings are chopped as they pass through the cutting module. The cut fibers of desired length (usually 0.5” to 1”) fall by gravity about 20-30” below on to a 2 conveying belt. Resin is fed to doctor boxes at the top and bottom locations. The doctor box has a fine opening through which the bulk resin forms a resin film as it moves on the conveying belt.
